conclusions: All four paired cases completed from identical physically generated first proposals replayed into independently owned Omega sessions. Every common first certificate failed unchanged exact acceptance. Neither DIRECT_REPAIR nor DIRECT_MODEL_REPAIR accepted any first or repaired candidate.

All 28 physical Super calls delivered complete JSON with known usage. No provider failure, retry, truncation, JSON syntax rejection, authority rejection, native execution or tool request occurred. This negative epoch cannot be attributed to unstable delivery.

Each arm used 16 allocated calls; physical inference was 28 calls because four shared first proposals were charged fully to both arms and physically generated once. Physical reported tokens were 73397; allocated reported tokens were 84418, including 11021 duplicated common-prefix tokens. Unknown logical and physical usage counts were zero.

The control submitted 16 rejected exact certificates. Treatment submitted 12 rejected exact certificates and spent four existing calls on public formulation: one structurally admitted unverified proposal and three formulation-contract rejections. The admitted proposal was actually used by a later call and still did not yield a correct certificate.

The three formulation-contract rejections are interface failures distinct from JSON syntax rejection and exact-answer rejection. Frozen telemetry does not identify whether problem binding, object shape, labels, assumptions or byte bounds caused them. Do not infer their precise field or call them mathematical failures.

All 28 allocated certificate output sets were complete. Their exact-string mismatches were not separately checked for mathematically equivalent noncanonical representations. All allocated certificate submissions reported confidence 1 and all failed exact acceptance. Confidence never overrides independent evaluation.

All eight arm/task stages reached unchanged exact acceptance; none was ungraded or unexecuted. Twenty-four distinct physical certificates were rejected; 28 allocated rejections include four replayed common-prefix certificates. Original first and later attempts remain separate with no ever-correct accumulation.

Treatment used 40221 allocated tokens versus 44197 control and no more calls, HTTP attempts or tokens in every pair. Only one pair met both the whole-stage and repair-only five-percent realized-token tolerance. Zero accepted outcomes cannot establish an efficiency or cognitive benefit.

Four fresh values in two already-known formal families, finite budgets and one admitted formulation exposure limit the result. No default, authority, official benchmark, broad reasoning, tool invention, procedure transfer or recursive-improvement promotion is supported.
